mainTopic: Roofing a סוכה with boards: the רב–שמואל מחלוקת, boards turned on their sides, and related ברייתות
overview: This amud is about roofing a סוכה with wooden boards (נסרים). It opens with the end of a ברייתא: two boards do not combine, but רבי מאיר says boards are like sheets and do combine. רב and שמואל disagree about which boards רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה argue over. שמואל says narrow boards, and רב says boards four טפחים wide. The גמרא explains how each of them reads the word 'combine.' A key idea is that boards can add up to four אמות next to a wall, the limit of the rule of דופן עקומה. The גמרא gives this explanation in two versions. Then it brings one ברייתא supporting רב, which includes רבי יהודה's story from a time of danger, and another supporting שמואל. Next, אמוראים argue about wide boards turned on their sides. רב נחמן rules they are פסול, like metal skewers, which leads to a short exchange between רב הונא and his students about asking for reasons. Finally, the גמרא tries to prove רב הונא's view from a ברייתא about a board with only three טפחים inside the סוכה, and rejects the proof.

steps.title: Boards do not combine, but רבי מאיר says they do
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends: two boards do not combine, while רבי מאיר holds that boards are like sheets and do combine.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two boards do not join together. רבי מאיר says: even boards are like sheets.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting a ברייתא. The first opinion says two boards on the סוכה roof do not add up together. רבי מאיר disagrees and says boards add up, just like sheets.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just before this line, the ברייתא said that sheets (סדינים) on the roof combine to reach the measure that makes a סוכה invalid. The first opinion says boards do not follow that rule. רבי מאיר says boards do follow it. The rest of this passage asks what 'combine' means here.

keyTerms.meaning: Boards or planks of wood
They join together, adding up to reach a measurement
Sheets of cloth
A תנא who is stricter about using boards as סכך

phrases.english: Two boards do not join together.
phrases.notes: End of the ברייתא's first opinion; sheets were said to combine just before this.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says:
Even boards are like sheets.
phrases.notes: Meaning: boards also join together toward the measure that makes the סוכה invalid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a ברייתא that began on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first opinion: boards do not combine. רבי מאיר: boards combine like sheets.

steps.title: The ברייתא fits שמואל's view easily
steps.stepSummary: For שמואל, the argument is about narrow boards, so 'combining' means narrow boards add up to four טפחים of invalid roofing.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for שמואל. He said the argument is about boards less than four טפחים wide, and that wide boards are invalid according to everyone. So 'combine' means the narrow boards add up to four טפחים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the ברייתא is easy to understand according to שמואל. This is a setup step: it prepares the challenge against רב in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For שמואל, a board four טפחים wide is invalid according to everyone, so רבי מאיר's strictness must be about narrower boards. Two narrow boards together can reach four טפחים, which makes the roof invalid. So the word 'combine' fits his view perfectly.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well for (sets up a contrast with a view that has a problem)
An אמורא who argues with רב about this case
A disagreement
According to everyone
Invalid, not kosher

phrases.english: It works well for Shmuel, who said:
When they are not four [handbreadths wide], there is a dispute,
but if they are four [handbreadths wide],
everyone agrees it is invalid,
what does 'join together' mean?
They join together to make four [handbreadths].
phrases.notes: Four טפחים of invalid roofing is enough to make the סוכה invalid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reads the ברייתא's word 'combine' according to שמואל's version of the מחלוקת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For שמואל, 'combine' means narrow boards add up to four טפחים.

steps.title: How can רב explain combining boards?
steps.stepSummary: For רב, the argument is about wide boards. But if they are wide, why would they need to combine? And if they are narrow, רב says they are kosher like reeds.
steps.simpleTranslation: But for רב, who said the argument is about boards four טפחים wide and that narrow boards are kosher according to everyone, what case is this? If each board is four wide, why would they need to combine? If they are less than four, why would they be invalid? They are just like reeds!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב. Neither possible case seems to fit the word 'combine'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Option one: the boards are wide. Then each board is already invalid by itself according to רבי מאיר, so combining adds nothing. Option two: the boards are narrow. Then רב himself says everyone treats them as kosher like ordinary reeds, so they cannot make the roof invalid at all. Either way, 'combine' seems to make no sense for רב.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who argues with שמואל
Valid, kosher
What is the case? What are the circumstances?
Why?
Just plain reeds

phrases.english: But for Rav, who said:
When they are four [handbreadths wide], there is a dispute,
but if they are not four [handbreadths wide],
everyone agrees it is valid,
what is the case?
If they are four [handbreadths wide],
why would they need to join together?
phrases.notes: Each wide board is already invalid by itself.

phrases.english: If they are not four [handbreadths wide], why [would they be invalid]?
Aren't they just plain reeds?
phrases.notes: For רב, narrow boards are no different from reeds, which are kosher סכך.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with step 2: what was easy for שמואל is hard for רב.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's version of the מחלוקת about boards
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both possible cases make 'combine' meaningless. Wide boards are already invalid alone, and narrow boards are kosher like reeds.

steps.title: The boards combine toward four אמות next to the wall
steps.stepSummary: For רב, the boards really are four טפחים wide. 'Combine' refers to adding up to four אמות of invalid roofing next to the wall.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, they are four טפחים wide. What does 'combine' mean? They combine to make four אמות from the side.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רב. The boards are wide, and 'combine' refers to a different measure: four אמות along the side of the סוכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Invalid roofing placed next to a wall is normally not counted against the סוכה, because of the rule of דופן עקומה (we view it as the wall bending over). That rule only works for up to four אמות. So wide boards placed by the wall do not ruin the סוכה alone, but together they can reach four אמות. That makes it invalid according to רבי מאיר. This removes the challenge against רב.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually, really (keeps the original case and reinterprets)
Four cubits, a much bigger measure than four טפחים
From the side, next to the wall
A 'bent wall': invalid roofing next to a wall is viewed as part of the wall

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל: boards combine to four טפחים in the middle of the roof. רב: wide boards combine to four אמות at the side, under the rule of דופן עקומה.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two measures. Four טפחים (handbreadths) is the amount of invalid roofing in the middle that ruins a סוכה. Four אמות (cubits) is the limit for invalid roofing next to a wall under דופן עקומה. רב's answer switches from the first measure to the second.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the ברייתא can fit both רב and שמואל, so it does not disprove רב's view.

phrases.english: Really, they are four [handbreadths wide],
and what does 'join together' mean?
They join together to make four cubits from the side.
phrases.notes: This refers to the rule of דופן עקומה, which allows up to four אמות of invalid roofing next to a wall.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3 by giving 'combine' a new meaning.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation: the case is kept (wide boards), and 'combine' is applied to a different measure.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Combine' meant adding up to four טפחים, which does not fit רב.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רב, 'combine' means wide boards add up to four אמות next to the wall, where דופן עקומה stops applying.

steps.title: Another version: שמואל's view works smoothly
steps.stepSummary: In the לישנא אחרינא, the גמרא first shows that for שמואל, 'combine' simply means the boards add up to four אמות of invalid roofing next to the wall.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another version: For שמואל it is fine. He said the argument is about boards less than four טפחים wide, and that boards four טפחים wide are invalid according to everyone. So what does 'combine' mean? It means they add up to four אמות from the side.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a second version of the discussion. It starts by saying שמואל's view fits easily, which sets up a question on רב in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, the word 'combine' is explained the same way for שמואל as it was for רב in the first version: the boards add up to four אמות from the side. The phrase 'בשלמא' tells us that this side causes no trouble. The real question is about to come.

keyTerms.meaning: Another version of the same discussion
It is understandable / granted (sets up a contrast)
From the side, meaning next to the wall
Everyone agrees

steps.confusionAlert: This is NOT a new argument. It is the same discussion told a second way. In both versions the difficulty is on רב. What changes is the problem. In the first version, רבי מאיר's word 'combine' seemed impossible for רב. In this version, 'combine' means four אמות from the side, and the problem is רבי יהודה's words 'do not combine' (next step).

phrases.english: Another version:
It is understandable according to Shmuel, who said
the dispute is about boards that are not four handbreadths wide,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל יֵשׁ בָּהֶן אַרְבָּעָה דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל פְּסוּלָה,
phrases.english: but if they are four handbreadths wide, everyone agrees it is invalid;
what does 'they combine' mean?
They combine to make four cubits from the side.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Retells the רב and שמואל exchange in a second version, starting with שמואל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For שמואל, 'מצטרפין' means the boards add up to four אמות of invalid roofing from the side.

steps.title: For רב, רבי יהודה's 'do not combine' seems pointless
steps.stepSummary: For רב, רבי מאיר's 'combine' makes sense, but רבי יהודה holds that even wide boards are kosher, so his 'do not combine' seems to mean nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: But for רב there is a problem. For רבי מאיר it is fine: 'combine' means they add up to four אמות from the side. But רבי יהודה says that even boards four טפחים wide are kosher. So what does 'they do not combine' mean? They are simply like reeds!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב's view. For רבי יהודה, the word 'do not combine' seems to have no purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב, רבי יהודה says wide boards are kosher סכך, just like reeds. Kosher roofing never becomes invalid by adding up, so there is nothing to 'combine' in the first place. That makes the phrase 'אין מצטרפין' seem meaningless.

keyTerms.meaning: They do not combine / add up
They are just ordinary reeds (fully kosher סכך)
Kosher, valid

phrases.english: But according to Rav:
it is understandable according to Rabbi Meir;
what does 'they combine' mean?
They combine to make four cubits from the side.
But according to Rabbi Yehuda, who said
that even if they are four handbreadths wide it is valid,
what does 'they do not combine' mean?
They are simply reeds!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with step 5: שמואל was fine, but רב runs into trouble.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's reading of רבי יהודה's words 'אין מצטרפין'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If wide boards are kosher like reeds, there is nothing invalid to add up. So saying they 'do not combine' is meaningless.

steps.title: רבי יהודה just echoed רבי מאיר's wording
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה said 'do not combine' only because רבי מאיר said 'combine'. It is a matching phrase, not a real legal point.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since רבי מאיר said 'they combine,' רבי יהודה said 'they do not combine.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question on רב. רבי יהודה's words are just a reply in matching language.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'אין מצטרפין' do not teach a separate rule for רבי יהודה. He simply answered רבי מאיר in his own terms, meaning 'I don't agree with you.' So רב's view stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Since [the other one] said it, this one also used that language

phrases.english: Since Rabbi Meir said 'they combine,'
Rabbi Yehuda said 'they do not combine.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 6.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every word in רבי יהודה's statement must carry its own legal meaning.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'אין מצטרפין' is only a mirror of רבי מאיר's language. It is not a separate rule.

steps.title: There are ברייתות supporting each side
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא announces that one ברייתא supports רב and another supports שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא was taught that supports רב, and a ברייתא was taught that supports שמואל.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא announces that it will bring a supporting source for each אמורא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now, רב and שמואל were each explaining the same ברייתא in their own way. Now the גמרא says each one has outside support, and it is about to quote those sources.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא was taught in agreement with him

phrases.english: It was taught in accordance with Rav,
it was taught in accordance with Shmuel.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּרַב, תַּנְיָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from explaining the words to bringing outside proofs.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each אמורא has a ברייתא that supports him.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רב: the argument is about wide boards
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says narrow cedar boards are kosher according to everyone, and the argument is only about boards four טפחים wide, just as רב said.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא supports רב: If someone covered his סוכה with cedar boards less than four טפחים wide, everyone agrees it is kosher. If they are four טפחים wide, רבי מאיר says it is invalid and רבי יהודה says it is kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that matches רב's view exactly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב said narrow boards are kosher like reeds, and the argument is only about wide boards. This ברייתא says the very same thing. That is the opposite of שמואל, who placed the argument on narrow boards.

keyTerms.meaning: He roofed it (covered the סוכה)
Cedar boards
Rules it invalid
Rules it valid

steps.whatToRemember: רב says: narrow boards are kosher according to everyone, and wide boards are the subject of the argument (רבי מאיר says invalid, רבי יהודה says kosher). A ברייתא supports this.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives רב's position direct textual support, so his view is not just a reading of the first ברייתא.

phrases.english: It was taught in accordance with Rav:
If one roofed it with cedar boards
that are not four handbreadths wide,
everyone agrees it is valid.
If they are four handbreadths wide,
Rabbi Meir rules it invalid
and Rabbi Yehuda rules it valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Carries out the first half of the announcement in step 8.
steps.raayaObject: רב's position that the argument concerns boards four טפחים wide, and that narrow boards are kosher

steps.title: רבי יהודה's story from a time of danger
steps.stepSummary: Inside the ברייתא, רבי יהודה brings a story to prove that boards four טפחים wide are kosher סכך.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said: There was an incident during a time of danger. We brought boards that were four טפחים wide, put them as roofing on top of a porch, and sat under them.
steps.whatsHappening: This continues the same ברייתא that supports רב. רבי יהודה tells a real-life story to prove that wide boards are kosher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה says he and others actually sat in a סוכה made of boards four טפחים wide. That suggests such boards are kosher סכך. This only works as proof if the argument is about wide boards, which is exactly רב's reading.

keyTerms.meaning: A time of danger, when the non-Jewish rulers banned מצוות
Boards or planks
A porch or balcony
We roofed it (put on the סכך)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said:
There was an incident in a time of danger
when we brought boards that were four handbreadths wide
phrases.notes: This is the key detail: the boards were the wide kind.

phrases.english: and we roofed over a porch with them,
phrases.notes: Doing it on a porch made it look less like a סוכה, which was safer.

phrases.english: and we sat beneath them!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: מַעֲשֶׂה בִּשְׁעַת הַסַּכָּנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא quoted in step 9 with רבי יהודה's proof for his own view.
steps.raayaObject: That boards four טפחים wide are kosher סכך, as רבי יהודה holds
steps.raayaSupportSource: A מעשה (actual practice) from a time of persecution

steps.title: The חכמים reject the story as proof
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים answer that what people did in a time of danger proves nothing about the normal law.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: You bring a proof from there? A time of danger is no proof.
steps.whatsHappening: The other חכמים push back on רבי יהודה's story. They say a time of danger is not a normal situation, so it cannot prove the law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a time of danger, people may build a פסולה סוכה just to remember the מצוה they cannot properly do. So the fact that they sat there does not show the boards were kosher. Taken as a whole, this ברייתא shows that the argument is about wide boards, which supports רב.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that a proof?! (a rejection)
It is no proof

steps.whatToRemember: The first ברייתא shows that רבי יהודה allows boards four טפחים wide, so the argument is about wide boards, just as רב said.

phrases.english: They said to him: Is there proof from there?!
A time of danger is no proof.
phrases.notes: What people do under persecution may only be a reminder of the מצוה, not a kosher fulfillment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי יהודה's proof from the story in step 10.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the story. It does not rule on the board law itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: An emergency situation is not normal, so what people did then does not show what is kosher.

steps.title: A ברייתא that supports שמואל
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא says wide boards are פסול according to everyone, and the argument is only about narrow boards.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in line with שמואל: If someone roofed the סוכה with cedar boards four טפחים wide, everyone agrees it is פסול. If they are less than four, רבי מאיר says it is פסול and רבי יהודה says it is kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא brings the second ברייתא it promised in step 8. This one supports שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the argument between רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה is moved down to narrow boards. Wide boards are פסול for everyone. That is the opposite of the first ברייתא, and it fits שמואל's view.

keyTerms.meaning: In line with him (supporting his view)
Cedar
Everyone agrees
Rules it פסול / rules it kosher

steps.confusionAlert: The two ברייתות really do disagree about where the argument is. In the first one it is about wide boards (רב). In this one it is about narrow boards (שמואל). Don't try to make them say the same thing.

phrases.english: It is taught in accordance with Shmuel:
If one roofed it with cedar boards

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהֶן אַרְבָּעָה — דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל פְּסוּלָה.
phrases.english: that are four handbreadths wide, everyone agrees it is unfit.
If they are not four wide,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי מֵאִיר פּוֹסֵל וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה מַכְשִׁיר.
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir deems it unfit and Rabbi Yehuda deems it fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the proof for רב, the גמרא brings the second ברייתא, which supports שמואל.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's view that the argument is about narrow boards, and that wide boards are פסול for everyone

steps.title: What each תנא agrees to
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds one point רבי מאיר agrees to and one point רבי יהודה agrees to.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר agrees that if the gap between boards is as wide as a board, you fill it with kosher roofing and the סוכה is kosher. רבי יהודה agrees that if a board four טפחים wide was placed on it, the סוכה is kosher, but you may not sleep under that board, and someone who sleeps under it has not fulfilled his obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: The same ברייתא continues. It shows where each side agrees with the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר does not throw out the whole roof. If the gaps are big enough to fill with real סכך, the סוכה works. רבי יהודה agrees that a wide board is not real סכך. The סוכה is still kosher (for example, the board is treated as part of the wall), but the space under the board does not count, so you cannot sleep there.

keyTerms.meaning: And he agrees
As wide as a full board
Leftover waste from the threshing floor or winepress, which is kosher סכך
Fulfilled his obligation

phrases.english: And Rabbi Meir concedes

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאִם יֵשׁ בֵּין נֶסֶר לְנֶסֶר כִּמְלֹא נֶסֶר —
phrases.english: that if between one board and the next there is the full width of a board,
one places kosher waste roofing between them, and it is fit.
And Rabbi Yehuda concedes
that if one placed on it a board
that is four handbreadths wide, it is fit,
phrases.notes: The סוכה as a whole stays kosher, for example by treating the board as a bent-over part of the wall.

phrases.english: but one may not sleep beneath it,

phrases.aramaic: וְהַיָּשֵׁן תַּחְתָּיו — לֹא יָצָא יְדֵי חוֹבָתוֹ.
phrases.english: and one who sleeps beneath it has not fulfilled his obligation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא that supports שמואל and adds each תנא's concession.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: narrow boards with board-wide gaps filled with פסל make a kosher סוכה. רבי יהודה: a board four טפחים wide is not real סכך, so you may not sleep under it, even though the סוכה stays kosher.
steps.whatToRemember: There is a ברייתא for each side: one supports רב (the argument is about wide boards), and one supports שמואל (the argument is about narrow boards).

steps.title: Argument about wide boards turned on their sides
steps.stepSummary: אמוראים argue about wide boards that were turned on their narrow edges.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was said: If one turned the boards on their sides, רב הונא says the סוכה is פסול, and רב חסדא and רבה בר רב הונא say it is kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question. A board is too wide lying flat, but on its edge it is narrow. Which way counts?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא says the board stays פסול because what matters is the board itself, which is wide. רב חסדא and רבה בר רב הונא say the board's position counts, and on its side it is narrow, so it is kosher.

keyTerms.meaning: It was said (introduces an argument between אמוראים)
He turned them onto their sides (narrow edges)
פסולה (invalid) / kosher

phrases.english: It was stated: If one turned them on their sides,
Rav Huna said: It is unfit,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב חִסְדָּא וְרַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא אָמְרִי: כְּשֵׁרָה.
phrases.english: and Rav Ḥisda and Rabba bar Rav Huna said: It is fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic about boards that are too wide, now placed on their edges.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב הונא: פסול. רב חסדא and רבה בר רב הונא: kosher.

steps.title: The question is brought to רב נחמן
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא and רבה בר רב הונא visit רב נחמן in סורא and ask him about boards turned on their sides.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן came to סורא. רב חסדא and רבה בר רב הונא went in to see him and asked: If one turned the boards on their sides, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that sets up the next step. The two who said 'kosher' ask a great authority to see whether he agrees with them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They ask without saying their own opinion, so they can hear רב נחמן's honest ruling. His answer will decide between them and רב הונא.

keyTerms.meaning: He happened to come
סורא, a major תורה center in בבל
What is the law?

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman happened to come to Sura,

phrases.aramaic: עוּל לְגַבֵּיהּ רַב חִסְדָּא וְרַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא.
phrases.english: and Rav Ḥisda and Rabba bar Rav Huna went in to him.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרִי לֵיהּ: הֲפָכָן עַל צִידֵּיהֶן, מַהוּ?
phrases.english: They said to him: If one turned them on their sides, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the argument from step 14 to רב נחמן for a ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether wide boards turned on their sides are kosher סכך

steps.title: רב נחמן rules: פסול, like metal skewers
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן rules the סוכה is פסול, because these boards are like metal skewers, which are never kosher.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: It is פסול. They have become like metal skewers.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers the question and sides with רב הונא. He gives a comparison to explain why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once a board has the status of סכך פסול, it stays פסול no matter how you turn it. It is like a metal skewer, which is פסול in any position because the material itself is not סכך.

keyTerms.meaning: Skewers or spits
Metal
They have become (taken on the status of)

steps.whatToRemember: Wide boards turned on their sides are still פסול, as רב נחמן ruled, following רב הונא.
steps.whyThisMatters: This teaches that a פסול item stays פסול by its status. Changing how you place it does not fix it.

phrases.english: He said to them: It is unfit,
they have become like skewers of metal.
phrases.notes: Metal is never kosher סכך, whether it is flat or on its side.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ: פְּסוּלָה, נַעֲשׂוּ כְּשַׁפּוּדִין שֶׁל מַתֶּכֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question asked in step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: פסול. Boards that are פסול as סכך keep that status even when turned on their sides, like metal skewers.

steps.title: רב הונא Says: Didn't I Tell You to Rule Like Me?
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא hears that רב נחמן ruled like him and tells his students they should have followed him from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said to them: Didn't I tell you to say the הלכה like me?
steps.whatsHappening: The two scholars report רב נחמן's ruling back to רב הונא. רב הונא points out that he had already told them this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רב הונא ruled that wide boards turned on their sides are פסול, and רב חסדא and רבה בר רב הונא disagreed. Now רב נחמן has agreed with רב הונא, so רב הונא says they should have accepted his ruling in the first place.

keyTerms.meaning: Like me, following my opinion
I told you

phrases.english: Rav Huna said to them:
Didn't I tell you
phrases.notes: A gentle rebuke to the two scholars who visited רב נחמן.

phrases.english: to rule like me?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַב הוּנָא: לָא אֲמַרִי לְכוּ אֱמַרוּ כְּווֹתִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reacts to רב נחמן's ruling in Step 16, which matches רב הונא's position.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב הונא's opinion (boards turned on their sides are פסול) is confirmed by רב נחמן.

steps.title: The Students Explain: רב נחמן Gave Us a Reason
steps.stepSummary: The scholars defend themselves: רב נחמן explained his reason, and that is why they accepted it.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Did you, master, ever tell us a reason that we then refused to accept?
steps.whatsHappening: The two scholars answer רב הונא's rebuke. They say they accepted רב נחמן because he gave a reason, and רב הונא never did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their point is that they did not ignore רב הונא out of stubbornness. רב נחמן explained that the boards are like metal skewers, and that reasoning convinced them. A bare ruling without a reason did not convince them.

keyTerms.meaning: The reason behind a ruling
Master (a respectful way to address a rabbi)
We accepted

phrases.english: They said to him:
And did the master tell us a reason
and we did not accept it from him?
phrases.notes: Meaning: רב נחמן gave us a reason, so we accepted it. You never gave one.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: וּמִי אָמַר לַן מָר טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to רב הונא's rebuke in Step 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why didn't you follow me from the start?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: You never gave us a reason. רב נחמן did, so we accepted his ruling.

steps.title: רב הונא Replies: You Never Asked Me for a Reason
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers that they never asked for his reason; if they had, he would have explained.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Did you ever ask me for the reason, and I refused to tell you?
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא answers his students' defense. The fault is theirs, because they never asked him why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא implies that he had the same reason all along. A student who disagrees should ask for the reasoning before rejecting a ruling. This closes the short story.

keyTerms.meaning: You asked / requested
From me

steps.whatToRemember: רב נחמן agrees with רב הונא: wide boards turned on their sides are פסול, because they are like metal skewers.

phrases.english: He said to them:
And did you ask me for the reason
and I did not tell you?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ: וּמִי בְּעֵיתוּ מִינַּאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the students' defense in Step 18 and closes the story.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The students never asked for a reason. Had they asked, רב הונא would have given it.

steps.title: A ברייתא That Might Support רב הונא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא listing invalid סוכות, including one with a four-טפחים board of which only three טפחים are inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this supports him? A סוכה is פסולה in these cases: it cannot hold a person's head, most of his body, and his table; or a breach opened in it big enough for a young goat to jump through headfirst; or a board four טפחים wide was placed on it, even though only three טפחים of the board are inside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a possible proof for רב הונא. It quotes a ברייתא; the key case is the last one, about the board.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The board is four טפחים wide, yet only three טפחים are inside the סוכה, and the סוכה is still פסולה. The next step will ask how a four-טפחים board could have only three טפחים inside. That question is what might link the ברייתא to רב הונא.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say this supports him?
His head, most of his body, and his table (the minimum size of a סוכה)
A breach or gap in a wall
Headfirst, in one leap
A board or plank

steps.confusionAlert: Only the last case (the board) matters for the proof. The first two cases are just part of the same list in the ברייתא.

phrases.english: Shall we say this supports him:

phrases.aramaic: אֵינָהּ מַחְזֶקֶת כְּדֵי רֹאשׁוֹ וְרוּבּוֹ וְשׁוּלְחָנוֹ,
phrases.english: A sukkah that does not hold his head, most of his body, and his table,
or one in which a breach was opened

phrases.aramaic: כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּזְדַּקֵּר בָּהּ גְּדִי בְּבַת רֹאשׁ,
phrases.english: large enough for a young goat to leap through headfirst,
or one on which he placed a board
that is four handbreadths wide,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא הִכְנִיס לְתוֹכָהּ
phrases.english: even though he brought into it
only three handbreadths — it is invalid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the story, the גמרא looks for a תנאי source that supports רב הונא.
steps.raayaObject: רב הונא's view that a wide board turned on its side is still פסול.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: a four-טפחים board with only three טפחים inside the סוכה still makes it פסולה.

steps.title: Explaining the Proof: The Board Was Turned on Its Side
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the ברייתא describes a board turned on its side, so it covers only three טפחים yet is still פסול, just like רב הונא says.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? Is it not where he turned the boards on their sides?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the ברייתא would prove רב הונא's view. It suggests the board was turned on its side, so its four-טפחים width now covers only three טפחים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a board lying on its side covers only three טפחים and the ברייתא still calls the סוכה פסולה, then the board's real width (four טפחים) is what counts. That is exactly רב הונא's position.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? How do we picture it?
Is it not that...? (introduces a suggested reading)
He turned them on their sides

phrases.english: What are the circumstances,
is it not where he turned them on their sides?
phrases.notes: If so, this would support רב הונא.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָּמֵי, מַאי לָאו כְּגוֹן שֶׁהֲפָכָן עַל צִידֵּיהֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the ברייתא in Step 20 would support רב הונא.
steps.raayaObject: רב הונא's ruling about boards turned on their sides.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's four-טפחים board with only three טפחים inside, read as a board turned on its side.

steps.title: Rejection: The Board Sticks Out Past the Doorway
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. The board lies over the doorway with three טפחים inside and one outside, and the part outside still counts as part of the סוכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Here we are dealing with a case where he placed the board over the entrance of the סוכה, with three טפחים inside and one טפח outside. The outside part is פסל sticking out of the סוכה, and any פסל sticking out of the סוכה is judged like the סוכה itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. It offers a different picture of the ברייתא that has nothing to do with turning boards on their sides.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The board lies flat over the doorway, where there is no wall. Three טפחים are inside and one טפח sticks out. Since פסל that sticks out is judged like the סוכה, the board counts as a full four טפחים of invalid covering, which makes the סוכה פסולה. So the ברייתא neither proves nor disproves רב הונא.

keyTerms.meaning: With what case are we dealing here? (introduces a narrower reading)
The entrance or opening of the סוכה
Invalid covering (material not fit for סכך)
Invalid covering that sticks out past the סוכה
Is judged as part of the סוכה

steps.confusionAlert: Placing the board over the doorway matters. Since there is no wall there, the rule of דופן עקומה (counting invalid covering as a bent wall) cannot help, so the board is treated as four טפחים of invalid covering.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא does not prove רב הונא. It can be read as a flat board over the doorway that sticks out by one טפח, and the outside part still counts.
steps.whyThisMatters: The גמרא often rejects a proof by reading the source as a different case. Here it also teaches a rule: invalid covering that sticks out past the סוכה is still judged as part of the סוכה.

phrases.english: No, with what are we dealing here?
For example, where he placed it over the entrance of the sukkah,
bringing three handbreadths inside
and taking one handbreadth outside,

phrases.aramaic: דְּהָוֵה לֵיהּ פְּסָל הַיּוֹצֵא מִן הַסּוּכָּה,
phrases.english: so that it is invalid covering sticking out of the sukkah,
and any invalid covering that sticks out of the sukkah
is judged like the sukkah.
phrases.notes: So the board counts as a full four טפחים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reading in Step 21 by offering a different case for the ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the ברייתא. רב הונא's ruling itself still stands.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the board was turned on its side. It may instead be a flat board over the doorway that sticks out one טפח, which counts as part of the סוכה.
